services and help the people and businesses of Vassalboro.
In a time when every district, every county, and every town is asking for funding, we appreciate
your consideration regarding this request.

Thank you,

Alicia Collins,

10037767:
REQUEST FOR RELIEF FOR THE VASSALBORO SANITARY DISTRICT
The Vassalboro Sanitary District, a quasi-municipal entity, was created in the 1970's to provide a public wastewater collection and treatment system to improve water quality in China Lake and Outlet Stream. The areas of North and East Vassalboro provided housing and labor for the woolen mill and sawmill in the towns. Homes were built on small, concentrated lots of land. Over time, private systems of sewer discharged untreated sewage to the local waterbodies. The private owners of these sewers were required by the Maine Department of Environmental Protection to provide acceptable treatment. With rigid enforcement of environmental laws required after the passage of the Clean Water Act, the sewer system was constructed due to most homes unable to dispose of wastewater in a conventional septic tank and subsurface bed due to the small lot sizes and poorly drained clay soil. Because the Town of Vassalboro did not own the sewer system, the town was shielded from enforcement action.
Several engineering studies were conducted during the 1960's and 1970's to solve the wastewater disposal issues. The general recommendation was to collect the wastewater and pump it to Winslow for treatment at the new Kennebec Sanitary Treatment District plant in Waterville. During the late 70's and 80's federal and state grants were made available to communities which covered 90% of the construction costs for wastewater treatment facilities. Vassalboro qualified for federal and state grant assistance during this time. During the late 1970's and early 1980's, the use of "alternative" technologies was encouraged and was funded at up to 100% grant funding. The Sanitary District eventually chose to construct an alternative system to maximize the project funding. This consisted of localized sewer systems and sand filtration beds with discharge to the Outlet Stream which connects China Lake to the Kennebec River. The sand filter beds did not perform as expected after construction, but the district was able to receive funding to correct the operational problems. However, the solution was to construct open sand filter beds which pumped partially treated sewage onto the ground surface to infiltrate through the sand filter beds. This met the treatment requirements but resulted in nuisance conditions due to the sewage on the ground surface in the middle of town.
After 30 years of use, the original wastewater treatment system was worn out and obsolete. In addition, the Maine DEP imposed more stringent treatment requirements which the older technology could not meet. The district was threatened with enforcement action if the system was not improved. In 2015, the district decided to upgrade the system by abandoning the old sand filter beds and connecting to the Winslow system. Had the district done this originally the cost of upgrading the system would have been far less than the nearly $9 million the new system eventually cost. The district was able to receive a significant amount of federal, state, and local funding for the project, but was still forced to borrow over $3 million to finance the project. Due to only a small number of users paying, the projected user fee was higher than the maximum that the Maine DEP considered to be an expensive project. The DEP guidelines allowed additional funding to be made available to the district. The district requested additional funding of $2,722,000 to help reduce the user fees and help keep costs affordable. Due to the number of other requests for grant funding, DEP awarded a grant of $600,000.
During project design and construction, the Town of Vassalboro helped facilitate: 1. TIF grants of $290,000 to be used toward the capital costs of the project. 2. The Town of Vassalboro applied for and received a Community Development Block Grant for $997,340 which was used toward the capital costs of the project.
Operational costs consist of paying the Town of Winslow a contract quarterly base fee of $1,212.19 plus customer rate of water usage, operation of the collection and pumping system within the Town of Vassalboro, and office personnel. Since the system began operation in 2018, operational costs have more than doubled and resulted in user costs which are the highest in the State of Maine. The village areas of North and East Vassalboro are some of the lowest income areas in town, and the resultant user charges of more than $2000 per year for a user are not sustainable.
The district is requesting relief to the project debt which consists of a federal loan of $2,113,000 and state loan of 1,445,775. Assistance with this debt will help reduce the user fees to a more sustainable level.

A consulting engineer hired by the District evaluated several options to achieve compliance and
concluded that connection to the Kennebec Sanitary Treatment District (KSTD) in Waterville, via the
Town of Winslow sewer lines, was the most cost-effective option based on estimated initial capital
costs and ongoing O&M costs identified in the feasibility report. During this evaluation, beyond the
phosphorous limit issue, the consulting engineer noted that the existing sand filter system had
reached the end of its useful life and had several other significant problems. The project to connect to the KSTD, via the Town of Winslow sewer lines, was completed in 2020.
The District and the Town of Vassalboro were proactive in moving the project forward and seeking
financial assistance from several entities for the eventual �~$7.6 million project. Although it took a few
years, a funding package was put together involving six federal and state funding sources. The
package resulted in grants of ~ $4.6 million and loans to the District of ~ $3.1 million (approximately

The DEP portion of this package was ~ $2.7 million, consisting of a $1.04 million Clean Water State
Revolving Fund (CWSRF) low interest loan, $1.049 million CWSRF principal forgiveness funding (no
repayment needed), and $600,000 State Grant.

10040955:
Christopher French Town of Vassalboro LD 832
Senator Lawrence, Representative Sachs, and respected members of the Energy, Utilities, & Technology Committee (E.U.T.C.), my name is Christopher J. French. I am the senior elected selectboard member representing the Town of Vassalboro. In addition to the time and consideration of the E.U.T.C has scheduled to review LD 832, I would like to extend my gratitude to Senator Bradstreet and Representative Collins, for their commitment to providing a resolution on behalf of the ratepayers of the Vassalboro Sanitary District (VSD/district). The rate payers of the district have been negatively impacted by untenable sewer rates directly tied to the cost of infrastructure improvements. This financial crisis has been compounded by generationally high inflation, increased cost of essentials including utilities, food, home heating, and the lack of available options in the means of affordable housing. Many of these families have no choice but to stay pat and attempt to navigate rising user fees associated with an unsurmountable debt service, rising district administrative costs, and increased user rates approved by the Town of Winslow, all spread across a very small number of rate payers. An alarming number of these homeowners are in crisis living on a fixed income, facing the reality of losing their homes through the legislative approved lien foreclosure process. I encourage the members of the E.U.T.C. to carefully review the facts of, and consider, the true impact LD 832 may have in relieving this financial quandary for those affected. The district has been a main stay for a small contingency of North & East Vassalboro residents along Route 32 and the Outlet stream for the past 50 years. Prior to the most recent construction the district relied on sand filters using the Outlet stream to carry the waste to the ocean. It is my understanding the district faced penalties due to non-compliance with the CLEAN WATER ACT and sought the advice of a contractor skilled in waste management. It was the contractor's recommendation, and least expensive method, to build out a system that connected to the Town of Winslow sewer district. It is my interpretation after reviewing information and project timelines made available to the selectboard that the unforeseen timing of COVID played a crucial role due to pandemic related spikes in construction expenses. Once the project had commenced the district found themselves in a no-win situation and what was once considered to be a manageable debt service quickly converted into the albatross the district currently experiences. In addition to the debt service, the user rates charged by the Town of Winslow continue to remain influx as our neighboring municipality attempts to manage their own infrastructure improvement costs that are passed down to the rate payers. From a ten-thousand-foot view, the Town of Vassalboro's current housing stock numbers sit roughly around 2200 structures, approximately 200 (9% of the housing stock) are within the district's jurisdiction. To assist with defraying the cost of the sewer project the Vassalboro selectboard recommended establishing a Tax Increment Financing (TIF) zone which included the provision of allocating money to the sewer district upgrade. In 2014 the voters of the Town of Vassalboro adopted the recommended TIF ordinance. Since the ordinance approval the town has assisted the district in securing funds in excess of $1.7 million through funding mechanisms such as Community Block Grants, TIF funding, and ARPA funding. Vassalboro's most recent contribution presented itself last year after the district requested consideration for TIF funds. The selectboard identified, to no fault of the districts, language connected with a prior selectboard approved TIF distribution amount of $100,000.00. Language became an obstacle for the district to use the money in any meaningful manner. The Selectboard recalled those funds and reallocated them in a way consistent with the DECD standards as well as authorizing the distribution of an additional $200,000.00 from the TIF to assist with debt services. As our Town Manager has frequently stated, the Town of Vassalboro and the District maintain a symbiotic relationship, shared common vision, and goals focused on

improving the water quality of the Outlet stream while properly managing unprocessed water. The town remains committed to assisting the district find a solution towards reducing the liability of its rate payers, however we are requesting that our partners at the State find a path through an extremely difficult budgeting process to provide relief for the rate payers and help prevent some of our more vulnerable citizens from losing their homes. I encourage the E.U.T.C. to take the necessary steps favorable to passing LD 832. Thank you for your consideration in this important matter.
Respectfully submitted, Christopher J. French Selectboard member, Town of Vassalboro

10037659:
Joint Standing Committee on Energy, Utilities, and Technology
RE: LD 832--An Act to Provide Funds to Reduce the Debt of the Vassalboro Sanitary District
Senator Lawrence, Representative Sachs, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Energy, Utilities, and Technology, my name is Dawn-Marie Nichols. I am a customer of the Vassalboro Sanitary District and a resident of Vassalboro, Maine . I appreciate this opportunity to testify in support of LD 832, a bill to provide one-time funding to the Vassalboro Sanitary District for debt reduction.
The astronomical increases in the Vassalboro Sanitary District fees and rates are debilitating to the finances of so many homes in Vassalboro. For my household, we are always at the minimum water usage, making our sewer bill on the minimum end of the scale, yet I pay more for my sewer than I do property taxes! We are a household of 3 with 2 full time working adults and a live at home college student. We are constantly making sacrifices in our lifestyle, and cutting things in our budget to try to adjust to the huge increases in the cost of being connected to the Vassalboro Sanitary District. I've picked up a 2nd job to help offset the cost of the sewer bills to our household. And with no end in sight on paying off this enormous debt it makes the outlook seem rather bleak. We have seen several neighbors putting their homes up for sale. Neighbors on a fixed income that simply no longer have enough money to live in their home with these additional costs. Another neighbor has recently lost her husband. I know from helping my own mother after the loss of my father, that my neighbor will lose a significant amount of income to her household with the loss of her husband's social security. I truly fear that with this income loss, being able to sustain the large sewer bill (even at minimum usage) will be too much for her, and this will be what drives her out of state to live the remainder of her days with one of her adult children, instead of in the home where she and her husband built their life and their family. It literally breaks my heart to see our senior neighbors struggling so much due to things out of their control.
Before all of these increases, due to forced system upgrades, there were already many households unable to keep up with their sewer bills. These increases are making that a larger percentage.
The 200 households connected to the Vassalboro Sanitary District simply should not bare the burden of this exorbitant system upgrade!
I urge you to vote for this bill which would provide much needed debt reduction to the 200 customers that rely on the services of the Vassalboro Sewer district.
Thank you for your time and I am willing to answer any questions the committee may have.

Dawn-Marie Nichols (207) 592-6609 309 Cemetery Street Vassalboro, ME 04989

I own two properties on the Vassalboro Sanitary District sewer line. One is my residence and the other is my business. The increase in our rates has been dramatic since the update to the system, and we are paying for our sewer rates based on our water usage rates. For example, if I water my lawn, I still end up paying for that amount of water in the sewer bill, even though it's not going down that drain. I am paying $800 a year in sewer bills for my two properties, which is double the original amount when I first bought the properties in 2014 and 2017. I watched out my window as the construction company spent hours digging the same hole every day, worked in the hole for about an hour, and then filled it in again for the rest of the day, only to dig it up again the next day. This went on for weeks. The bill for this work (under Route 32, which is a state road) is paid for by the 200 people on the sewer line. It is impossible for us to afford this, and we have no choice but to be connected to the sewer line.
186114:
Richard Bradstreet THE MAINE SENATE 3 State House Station Senator, District 15 132nd Legislature Augusta, Maine 04333
March 18, 2025
LD 832: RESOLVE, TO ALLOCATE FUNDS TO REDUCE THE DEBT OF THE VASSALBORO SANITARY DISTRICT.
Senator Lawrence, Representative Sachs and the distinguished members of the Committee on Energy, Utilities and Technology, my name is Dick Bradstreet. I represent Senate District 15, which includes Augusta, Belgrade, China, Mount Vernon, Sidney and my hometown ofVassalboro, and I'm here today to present LD 832, a Resolve, to Allocate Funds to Reduce the debt of the Vassalboro Sanitary District.
First, a little bit of history: Several years ago, the septic system of the Vassalboro Sanitary District failed, and the District was forced to find a new method of disposing of septic waste. After searching through several options, the logical choice was to connect to the system that Winslow uses. Upon getting pricing and arranging financing, the VSD was hit with the perfect storm. I'd like to point out here that when I worked with the Department of Environmental Protection, which helped oversee the project, I found out that the proposal was right at the very top of the affordability metrics, which in itself was a daunting challenge for a District that has just 223 users. Then, as the project was underway, COVID hit and all pricing skyrocketed. The costs ended up way over budget, but at that point in time there was no turning back.
State House: (207) 287-1515 * Fax: (207) 287-1585 * Toll Free: 1-800-423-6900 * TTY: 711 Dick.Bradstreet@legislature.maine.gov * legishture.maine.gov/seiiate

The project has been completed, some grant funding was provided and the TownofVassalborohas pitched into help as best it can, but there still remain two loans which were a little over $2 million dollars each. Even though the interest rates on the loans are low, the repayment amounts that are passed onto the users in many cases exceed their real estate taxes. It is an untenable situation.
I approached the Governor's office seeking help, and was directed to the DEP in hopes there would be unused funds from other projects that could be transferred to help the VSD. The people there were very helpful, but unfortunately there were no such funds, and I also learned that once a project is funded, there is virtually no chance to go back and request more funds. I also contacted the office of Senator Collins, and I believe there is hope that some federal monies will be coming in the next fiscal year, but in all probability, if there are any, the amount will probably not exceed around $250,000 - way too little to provide real relief to the District. I should also point out that the Vassalboro Sanitary District is an independent entity and not a part of the Town of Vassatboro.
As you may well imagine, this dilemma is causing a lot of stress to those who are tied into the VSD. The costs are impoverishing many of the users, who are having a horrible time trying to make ends meet. Several are older people on fixed incomes, and there is just no way they can continue down this road. I understand that many of them may be facing foreclosure due to the fact that they can't pay all their bills, including their property taxes. Nobody is interested in buying their homes once they find out the monthly amount of the sewer bill, and nobody will purchase land to build a home that could be tied into the system, because the costs would be so exorbitant. To add to their woes, Winslow is looking to upgrade their system and the result of that will be even higher usage fees passed on to the VSD users.
I know this is an unusual request and I would not be making it if the situation were not so dire. I asked for the $2 million dollars in hopes that one of the loans could be paid off. Even after that, the remaining costs will still be

very high, but at least there would be tight at the end of the tunnel for these fellow Mainers. I do realize that many of our citizens are having a difficult time in making ends meet - housing that is affordable, paying for heat, feeding their families and a host of other challenges. But for most of those people, there are programs that help provide for what they need. For the people of the Vassalboro Sanitary District, there is none of that, and their only legitimate hope is that you will vote this bill out as "Ought to Pass," and that is what I hope you will do. The people who are suffering from this could certainly use a little good news. Thank you for your time.
Senator Dick Bradstreet
10037345:
Vassalboro LD 832
My husband and I purchased our home in Vassalboro in July of 2021. What should have been an exciting experience for us became a constant struggle, shortly after. Upon our first sewage bill of $450+, we found out that this is a normal quarterly bill. A quarterly bill that we have struggled immensely to pay. We have had to place our home in a forbearance, we have struggled to keep food on the table. We have had to put home repairs off due to having to prioritize our astronomical sewer bill every three months. This is not including the water bill. On top of this, we have had sewage back-ups, basement flooding and many letters sent to our home (along with all of Vassalboro) explaining how delicate this multi-million-dollar sewage system is. For something that costs so much, you would think that it would work flawlessly. I have been in risk of having a lean placed on my home many times and still struggle to pay it even 60 days past due.
My husband and I have decided to put our home up for sale due to the sewer situation. The cost of living on a normal circumstance is outrageous enough. This added expense is off the charts and we will not be victim of it any more. We have spoken with neighbors and friends of ours that reside in Vassalboro who are also placing their homes for sale due to the same reason. Vassalboro is dying off because of the cost of this single bill each quarter.
It's a shame that families have to lose the American dream due to unknowingly becoming responsible for a purchase that we never agreed to or knew we were getting into. It's criminal. It should be mandatory to proactively disclose the sewer cost to all residents and/or future residents!
10037714:
tara Karczewski-Mitchell Augusta LD 832
Joint Standing Committee on Energy, Utilities, and Technology RE: D832- An Act to Provide Funds to Reduce the Debt of the Vassalboro Sanitary District
Senator Lawrence, Representative Sachs, and members of the joint committee on Energy, Utilities, and Technology, my name is Tara Karczewski-Mitchell, and I am a customer of the Vassalboro Sanitary District and a resident in Vassalboro, Maine. I appreciate this opportunity to testify in support of LD 832, to provide one-time funding to the Vassalboro Sanitary District for debt reduction.
You have likely heard the back story about how we got here so I'll spare you the details. The Vassalboro Sanitary District was informed that they would be fined daily until the issue was rectified. Unfortunately, they proceeded with the project with only some of the money but not all and when I say all I'm talking about millions of dollars. Through research I have learned that getting money after a project has started or has finished is very difficult. This oversight shouldn't burden approximately 200 of its customers! I want to be clear LD 382 is to help the Vassalboro Sanitary District with debt reduction however at the end of the day 200 customers are expected to foot this massive bill. We are talking about millions! In Fall of 2023, a small group of us banned together. We were able to organize multiple meetings with the town, the Vassalboro Sanitary District, many of our neighbors negatively impacted. multiple political affiliates were invited which some did participate and some kindly declined. We started a petition to see if the town would consider this a town issue vs an issue that only 200 families were struggling with. This unfortunately, didn't resolve the issue. We contacted lawyers and reached out to multiple legal resources which didn't help. Please refer to the local newspapers in 2023 and 2024 to see our efforts. We contacted the media to keep the pressure on anyone and/or any entity that would help our cause. Everyone said no or sorry we can't help. What I can tell you is that Vassalboro is not known for its wealth and the areas that this negatively impacts are some of the poorest. What I also know is that I purchased my home approximately 14 years ago. Since then, my taxes have doubled, and my sewer bill is more than my taxes!!! When I moved in, I believe I was paying $140 quarterly and now for a family of two I am paying $350 quarterly. What are families of 4+ paying?? The increases throughout the years have been astronomical. I have calculated that we are paying 300% more than any other town in Maine and 60% more than the national average. When I was more actively involved with this issue 35% of us were late with our payments and there were multiple liens. There is no way after the last increase or two that these numbers have not sky rocketed. In 2023 and 2024 I said is that these financial obligations/decisions are of no fault of its customers, but we will be held accountable, and this bill is not sustainable for most of us. Vassalboro residents need your help in order to keep our properties. The folks that rent need your help so the landlords can charge a reasonable monthly rate.
I urge you to vote for this bill which would provide much needed debt reduction to the 200 customers that rely on the services of the Vassalboro Sanitary District.
Thank you for your time and I'm willing to answer any questions the committee may have.
Respectfully,
Tara Karczewski-Mitchell 207-441-9186
